summary: The starter prompt plus the provided run environment (skill_md) and installed DocumentDB skills are enough to start building the Node.js/Mongoose portfolio service. Several implementation details (exact schema fields, driver versions, change-stream options, webhook payload/recording, seed data and run/test instructions, and repository README/fixtures) are not specified and will be chosen by the builder as reasonable defaults unless the author states otherwise.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js Mongoose portfolio service that stores positions and alert rules in DocumentDB. Open a change stream on the positions collection to detect price updates, evaluate each alert rule document, and fire a webhook when a threshold is breached. Include an aggregation that computes portfolio P&L and sector allocation."
rubric.note: Prompt clearly defines the app purpose, the collections involved, reactive change-stream behavior, and the aggregation requirement.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Assume a single, long-running Node.js service (no agent framework) that runs change streams and exposes HTTP endpoints.
rubric.note: Prompt does not say whether to build via an agent, CI orchestration, or simply produce a standalone sample app.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js Mongoose" (starter prompt) and skill_md: Node.js 24 is available on the run environment.
rubric.note: Runtime constraint in skill_md: Node.js 24 with npm/npx available.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will pick a recent stable Mongoose that is compatible with MongoDB 7.0 (e.g., Mongoose 7.x with the mongodb driver 5.x). Code will use current Mongoose API and a singleton MongoClient pattern.
rubric.note: Installed documentdb-driver skill covers connection pattern (singleton) but does not mandate package versions.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable... use database named `sample_fintech_03`. Connection string in env var DOCUMENTDB_URI."
rubric.note: The run environment explicitly provides the cluster details and connection URI variable; builder must use that cluster and DB name.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder."
rubric.note: Secrets handling is explicitly constrained in skill_md.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores positions and alert rules in DocumentDB" (prompt) — no schema fields listed.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create two Mongoose models, Position and AlertRule, with fields sufficient for alert evaluation: Position { userId, symbol, shares:Number, avgCost:Number, currentPrice:Number, sector:String, updatedAt:Date, schemaVersion } and AlertRule { userId, scope:('symbol'|'global'), symbol?, metric:('price'|'pnl'), comparison:('>'|'<'), threshold:Number, webhookUrl:String, active:Boolean, createdAt }.
rubric.note: The documentdb-data-modeling skill gives modeling patterns but does not specify exact field names/required fields; the reference requirements list the preferred fields (and the builder will most likely adopt them).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include a small idempotent seed script (e.g., seed.js) that inserts a few example positions and alert rules and can be safely re-run (upsert or dedupe by a unique key). Typical seed size: handful of users, ~10 positions, a few alert rules.
rubric.note: Prompt does not mention sample data or a seed script. documentdb-local-deployment gives best practices but no concrete seed data.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Include an aggregation that computes portfolio P&L and sector allocation" and "Open a change stream on the positions collection" (prompt).
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement the aggregation using Mongoose.aggregate() to compute total P&L and per-sector market values and percentages. Reasonable indexes: single-field indexes on userId and on symbol; possibly a compound index on { userId:1, symbol:1 } and an index on sector for efficient grouping. Change streams do not require special indexes but code will use fullDocument updateLookup to get the latest document.
rubric.note: Index guidance exists in the documentdb-indexing skill, but the prompt does not demand any specific indexes or index parameters.
No embeddings or other AI components are requested by the starter prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js Mongoose portfolio service" and "Include an aggregation that computes portfolio P&L and sector allocation."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will expose a small HTTP API (Express) with at least GET /portfolio/:userId/summary returning { totalPnl, sectors:[{ sector, marketValue, percentage }] }. The service will also run the background change-stream listener to evaluate alerts.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for a service but does not enumerate endpoints; the reference expects GET /portfolio/:userId/summary.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: existing cluster reachable; "Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use."
rubric.note: Use the provided live cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and do not create new Azure resources for the sample run.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add README with commands: npm install; npm run seed (or node scripts/seed.js); npm start; and example curl to call GET /portfolio/:userId/summary. Tests: unit tests (jest) for aggregation logic; integration runnable if DOCUMENTDB_URI set.
rubric.note: skill_md provides runtime constraints but no run/test commands; these must be created by the builder.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat 'done' as: app connects to sample_fintech_03 using DOCUMENTDB_URI; Mongoose models are defined; change stream watches positions with fullDocument, detects price changes, queries alert rules, and sends POST webhooks; aggregation endpoint returns correct total P&L and sector allocations for a sample user; a seed script loads sample data; logs/README show what was executed.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in prompt; the above will be used as practical completion criteria.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture... Do not provision another cluster unless allowed."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid storing secrets in code, will not attempt provisioning, will not fully productionize security (e.g., no CMK, no Private Endpoint) but will note them in README as non-goals for the sample.
rubric.note: Security constraints about secrets and cluster provisioning are stated; cost/production constraints are not fully specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: recommends `.env.example` placeholders and not storing the real connection string.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will follow common sample repo layout: README.md, package.json, src/ (app code), scripts/seed.js, .env.example, tests/, and comment code with references to Azure DocumentDB. README will include setup/run/cleanup.
rubric.note: Prompt/skill_md instruct .env.example usage but does not mandate full repository layout; builder will adopt a conventional layout.

contradictions: Prompt says 'Using the DocumentDB skill' but there is no single installed skill named exactly 'DocumentDB skill' — the environment contains several documentdb-* skills (documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection, etc.). The builder will interpret this as 'use the available DocumentDB-related skills/guidance'.
questions_for_author: Which Mongoose and mongodb driver versions should be used (or should the builder pick the latest stable versions compatible with MongoDB 7.0)?
How should webhook deliveries be handled on failure? (e.g., single attempt with logging, retry policy with backoff, or push into a durable 'webhook deliveries' collection to retry later?)
Do you require a seed script and README as part of the delivered sample (the reference gallery typically expects them)? If so, any required minimal dataset size or example users to include?
requirements_at_risk: Exact Mongoose model fields for positions and alert rules (starter prompt mentions collections but not the required fields). Reason: prompt does not enumerate schema fields; no installed skill provides the exact field list.

Change stream option 'fullDocument: "updateLookup"' and explicit change-stream configuration. Reason: prompt asks to open a change stream but does not state fullDocument option; installed skills provide connection guidance but not this specific option.
Price-change detection detail (only trigger evaluation on currentPrice change vs any update). Reason: prompt says detect price updates but not the exact update-event filtering logic.

Alert rule metric types and evaluation semantics (must support both 'price' and 'pnl' with pnl computed as (currentPrice - avgCost) * shares). Reason: prompt says evaluate rules but does not enumerate metric types or formula; no skill supplies this exact rule set.

Webhook payload schema and storing webhook delivery status. Reason: prompt says 'fire a webhook' but does not detail payload contents or whether to persist HTTP status; no installed skill prescribes the payload.

HTTP endpoint contract (GET /portfolio/:userId/summary returning total P&L and sector allocations). Reason: prompt asks for the aggregation but does not explicitly require an HTTP endpoint and route; reference requires it.
Idempotent seed script that can be run twice without duplicating data. Reason: prompt does not request seed scripts; local-deployment skill provides best practices but no concrete seed artifact.
Pinned dependency versions (e.g., package.json lock or explicit pinned versions). Reason: prompt does not ask to pin dependencies.
Unit tests that run without a live cluster. Reason: prompt does not require tests and no skill provides automated unit-test scaffolding for offline tests.

Infrastructure-as-code for provisioning the DocumentDB cluster (Bicep/Terraform). Reason: prompt assumes an existing cluster and does not request IaC; reference may expect provisioning code but prompt forbids creating another cluster.
README covering what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up. Reason: prompt does not mention README; builder will likely add one but it's not specified.
